old_value: {"id":"project-LICHEN-worker6-4w24","title":"tunnel_auth check_time never advances last_now on the Ok path: rollback detection lags real time on a quiet gateway","description":"Found by security codereview of project-LICHEN-worker6-k8ix (P1). rust/lichen-gateway/src/tunnel_auth.rs check_time:419-430 updates self.last_now only on the fully-successful tails (accept_post:361, authorize_decapsulation:415), so the watermark is the time of the last SUCCESSFUL operation, not the last OBSERVED time. Python's mirror _observe_time (tunnel_auth.py:413) sets _last_now = now on EVERY non-rollback observation, including requests that later fail. On a low-traffic LoRa border router the watermark can lag real time unboundedly (and failing requests at real time never move it in Rust, while they would in Python); if the clock then rolls back to T with last_now \u003c= T, the rollback is undetected and any entry that expired in real time but was not yet opportunistically purged authorizes decapsulation again - the captured-grant-cannot-rearm guarantee is void exactly when the gateway is quiet. Fix: set self.last_now = Some(now) on the Ok path of check_time (the tail assignments become redundant but harmless); keep the rollback path NOT updating last_now (retain the high-water).","status":"open","priority":1,"issue_type":"bug","owner":"mark@reviewcommit.com","created_at":"2026-08-30T23:19:40.830007365Z","created_by":"opencode-worker-2","updated_at":"2026-08-30T23:19:40.830007365Z","dependencies":[{"issue_id":"project-LICHEN-worker6-4w24","depends_on_id":"project-LICHEN-worker6-k8ix","type":"discovered-from","created_at":"2026-08-30T23:19:40.946090731Z","created_by":"opencode-worker-2","metadata":"{}"}]}
